newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's UES invites banks to tender for bonds.
newsitem.headline: Russia's UES invites banks to tender for bonds.

text.p: Russia's national power company Unified Energy System(UES) said on Friday it had invited Western and domestic banks to submit bids to manage its issue of about $1 billion in convertible bonds.

UES chief executive Boris Brevnov told a news conference that Salomon Brothers, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, JP Morgan, Merrill Lynch, CS First Boston, ING, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, ABN Amro and Russia's SBS Agro were among those invited.
Brevnov said the banks had two weeks to submit their bids. The issue would cover up to five percent of the company's shares, including a 2.7 percent government stake.
Previous announcements had said slightly over five percent of shares of RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES) would be covered.
UES board member Vladimir Sidorovich said the proceeds from the sale of the bonds, which will have a maturity of around three years, would be used to develop regional networks and capacity.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Renaissance Capital were mandated on Thursday to lead manage UES's placement of at least $200 million of Eurobonds later this year.

UES, included in the drive to restructure the country's powerful natural monopolies, is Russia's largest company by sales, owns and operates the country's national power grid, and owns controlling stakes in most regional power plants.
